name: Metal platform bed frame
tagline: Steel side rails, bolt-on legs, and a roll of slats. No box spring needed.
peopleNote: Doable alone. Easier with two for the final lift.

tools.why: Some frames use nuts that need holding while you turn the bolt.
Steel tubes often arrive with machine oil on them.

before: Build it in the bedroom. An assembled queen frame does not fit through a standard door.
Have the mattress nearby but leaning against a wall, not on the floor where you need to work.
Lay a towel or the cardboard down. Steel rails scratch hardwood instantly.
safety: Steel edges from the factory can be sharp. Wipe the oil off and watch your fingers on cut ends.
Never skip the center support legs on a queen or king. That is what stops the frame from folding in the middle.

steps.title: Unpack and sort into three piles
steps.say: Make three piles. Long rails, short rails and legs, and the hardware bag. Wipe the oil off the steel now rather than onto your sheets later.
do: Two long side rails
Two short head and foot rails, plus legs
One hardware bag: bolts, washers, Allen key
steps.tip: The hardware bag is often taped inside one of the tubes. Shake them if you cannot find it.

steps.title: Lay the rectangle out on the floor first
steps.say: Put the four rails on the floor in the shape of the bed before you attach anything. Long rails on the sides, short ones at the head and foot.
do: Form the rectangle roughly where the bed will live
Point the bracket holes inward and up
Check the head rail is the one with the headboard bolt holes, if your frame has them
steps.watch: Head and foot rails can look identical but only one has the extra holes for a headboard. Compare them side by side.

steps.title: Bolt the corners finger-tight only
steps.say: Put every corner bolt in with its washer, but only finger-tight for now. Leaving them loose lets the frame shuffle into square.
do: Washer always goes between the bolt head and the steel
Thread each bolt in by hand several turns
Four corners, loose
steps.tip: Tightening as you go is why frames end up with one bolt that will not reach its hole. Loose first, tight last. Every single time.
steps.watch: If a bolt will not start by hand, you are cross-threading it. Back it out and start again straight.

steps.title: Fit the center support bar
steps.say: Queen and king frames have a bar that runs down the middle, head to foot. It bolts to the head and foot rails. This is the backbone.
do: Run it from head rail to foot rail through the center
Bolt both ends finger-tight
If it comes in two halves, join them in the middle first
steps.watch: Some frames have a second cross bar. Check the manual for how many — missing one is the usual cause of a frame that sags under a mattress.

steps.title: Screw the legs in
steps.say: Legs either thread into a socket or bolt onto a plate. Get them all in, including the center legs, which are the ones that actually carry the weight.
do: Thread each leg in until it stops
Center legs go on the support bar
Count them against the manual: there are usually more than you expect
steps.tip: If a leg has a plastic foot, make sure it is pressed fully on. They fall off and then the frame rocks.

steps.title: Square it, then tighten everything
steps.say: Measure both diagonals of the rectangle and nudge until they match. Now go around and tighten every bolt firmly. Corners first, then the center.
do: Measure corner to corner both ways
Push the long corner in until the numbers match
Tighten all bolts in a circuit, then do a second lap
steps.tip: A second lap matters: tightening one bolt loosens its neighbor. Two laps and it is solid.

steps.title: Roll out the slats
steps.say: Unroll the slats across the frame and space them evenly. Most have straps and a screw or clip at each end to stop them sliding.
do: Unroll from head to foot
Space them evenly along the frame
Secure the end slats with the screws or clips provided
steps.watch: Slats that are not fixed down creep toward the foot of the bed over a few months and then you have a gap under your hips.

steps.title: Shake it hard before the mattress goes on
steps.say: Grab a corner and rock it firmly. Any knock or squeak is a loose bolt, and it is ten times easier to find now than at midnight.
do: Push and rock each corner
Listen for a metallic knock
Chase the noise and tighten that bolt
steps.tip: Most squeaky metal bed complaints are one under-tightened bolt or a missing washer, not a bad frame.

steps.title: Mattress on, then set it against the wall
steps.say: Walk the mattress on from the foot end. Then slide the whole bed into place and check it sits level and does not rock.
do: Lift from the foot, not the side
Center it on the slats
Slide into position and check for rocking on uneven floors
steps.tip: If it rocks on an uneven floor, a folded piece of cardboard under one leg fixes it permanently and costs nothing.

fixes.q: The last bolt hole will not line up
fixes.a: Classic sign you tightened as you went. Loosen every other bolt a couple of turns, the frame will shuffle, the bolt will go in, then re-tighten everything.

fixes.q: The bed squeaks when I move
fixes.a: Do a full tightening lap. If it still squeaks, the usual culprits are a missing washer, slats rubbing on the rail — put felt pads or a strip of fabric under the slat ends — or the frame touching the wall.

fixes.q: The center sags under the mattress
fixes.a: A center support leg is missing or not touching the floor. Check every leg contacts the ground; some thread in and out to adjust height.

Check for a second cross support or extra legs you skipped, and check whether your frame also supports a headboard. Manufacturers do include a few spares, but count against the manual before assuming yours are spare.

fixes.q: My frame came with no slats
fixes.a: Some platform frames are designed for a bunkie board or a bed base instead. Check the listing. Putting a mattress straight onto bare rails voids most mattress warranties.
